assessment.text: The premise holds with real room: even the tightest quarter, Q1 FY2026, clears the 3% line by 0.7 percentage points, which is 5.09x a typical quarter-to-quarter move, and the same test held in 19 of 20 filing-date readings.

The stability comes from offsetting parts, not a steady business mix: gross margin took 0.2 percentage points off the year-on-year change while lower operating expenses relative to revenue added 0.3 percentage points, consistent with the flat annual cost ratios in the 10-K.
A 3% floor is a low bar for this decision, because the margin has moved only between 3.5% and 4.0% over eight quarters and still ranks 9 of 9 among SIC 5331 filers.

Holding at the 2026-09-30 price is where the claim stops helping: at a constant 3.8% margin, that price needs revenue growth of 17.3% a year for 10 years, against +6.6% a year over the last three fiscal years, and 0 of 44 comparable-size filers managed that pace.

The margin is the assumption the implied growth leans on most: at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 10.1% the same price needs only 2.9% a year. The claim shows the margin holding near 4.0%, not moving toward that level.
So the claim is true and shows the margin is durable, but it does not carry a decision to hold at this price, which depends on growth or a margin change the record does not show.

case_for.text: The implications of the claim all check out. The fiscal 2026 margin clears 3% by 0.9 points and is above fiscal 2025, and in the latest quarter operating income grew 2.7 points faster than revenue, which itself rose +11.1%.
Resampling the margin's own past quarterly changes kept the test intact in 100% of paths. That reflects how small the moves have been, not a forecast.
Stock compensation is steady at 0.3% of revenue, so the reported margin is not being flattered by a shift toward stock pay.

case_against.text: Gross margin is drifting down, and the filing itself names commodity prices and inflation as margin risks, so the floor relies on continued expense leverage.

Investors are paying 45.7x earnings for a 2.2% free cash flow yield, for a margin that sits below every industry peer counted, so a margin that merely holds is already in the price rather than a reason for it.
Margin durability says nothing about the 17.3% growth the price needs. The record cannot show whether the latest quarter's +11.1% revenue growth will last.

decides.text: The decision turns less on the 3% floor than on whether the operating margin breaks out of its 3.5% to 4.0% range, since the price is far more sensitive to margin than to the claim's threshold.
It also turns on whether expense leverage keeps offsetting gross-margin erosion; later quarterly bridges would show which way that is going.

would_change.text: A quarterly operating margin below 3% in any of the next four quarters would break the claim's test.
An operating margin below the eight-quarter low of 3.5% would show the room of the test shrinking toward the line.
An SG&A ratio back above the fiscal 2025 level of 9.25% would remove the expense leverage that has offset gross-margin slippage.

The thin margin does not point to weak earnings quality, since operating cash flow ran well above net income. Almost all of that excess was absorbed by capital expenditure, so whether the test holds is mainly a question of how much the company spends.
Management's stated intention to lift capital expenditure to about $7,500 in fiscal 2027 bears directly on a test with only $156.0M of room, unless operating cash flow rises at least as much.

assessment.text: In the only peer set the record holds, SIC 5331 filers with at least $100.0M of revenue, Costco ranked 4 of 9 in 2025 at 8.2% against a class median of 7.2%, so it outgrew the typical peer but not the three fastest.
A year earlier it held the same rank with 5.0% growth, equal to the class median of 5.0%, so the edge over the median rests on a single year rather than a sustained record.
The peer ranking stops at 2025, so the record cannot say whether the stronger fiscal 2026 growth of +11.1% in the newest quarter widened the lead or simply matched an industry-wide rise.

Some of the headline growth is not demand: gasoline added 130 basis points and currency 49 basis points, and comparable sales excluding them grew 7% in 2026 against 8% in 2025, so underlying growth slowed even as reported growth rose.

The step from beating peers to holding at this price is the weak link: at the 2026-09-30 price the reverse DCF needs 17.3% a year for 10 years, against the company's own +6.6% a year over three fiscal years, and 0 of 44 comparable-size spans grew that fast.

That price leans more on margin than on growth: at the industry median operating margin of 5.0% instead of 3.8% the need falls to 13.0% a year, so outgrowing peers, even if true, does not by itself carry the hold decision.

case_for.text: Growth was high and steady through fiscal 2026, at +9.2%, +11.6% and +11.1% in successive quarters, well above the 2025 class median of 7.2%.
The growth looks like sell-through rather than stocking: the newest quarter cleared the 5% bar by 6.1 points, and inventory did not outrun revenue, by a margin of -4.4 points.

thresholds.note: restates a threshold: 5% (cor:c4:1); not checked as a fact

case_against.text: Growth slowed by 0.5 percentage points from the prior quarter, the corollary the claim implies failed, and the underlying comparable-sales rate fell from 8% to 7%.

Costco itself warns that some competitors have greater technology capabilities and market penetration and that it could lose market share, which the record cannot test against peer figures after 2025.
Revenue billed ahead of delivery grew +5.3% against revenue's +11.1%, so the forward-booked part of the business is growing at half the headline pace.

decides.text: Whether the nine SIC 5331 filers are the right peers at all, since an SEC industry code can be a poor set and Costco ranked only 4 of 9 within it.
Whether a 2026 peer ranking, once filed, keeps Costco above the class median on growth excluding gasoline and currency effects.
Whether margin rather than growth moves toward what the price needs, since the implied growth falls to 2.9% a year at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 10.1%.

would_change.text: Quarterly operating margin reaching the industry median of 5.0% would cut the growth the price needs to 13.0% a year, shifting the decision from growth to margin.
A fourth-quarter revenue in fiscal 2027 below the $95.72B of Q4 FY2026 would mean revenue no longer grows, undercutting any claim of outgrowing peers.
A results 8-K reporting comparable sales excluding gasoline and currency below the 7% of 2026 would extend the underlying slowdown.

brief.summary: Two of four claims are Supported. Membership fees grew 11% to $5,907 versus 10.1% total revenue growth to $303.15B. The fee increase's share of that growth is fading (about 30% in 2026, from 40% in 2025), but 92.3% U.S./Canada and 89.8% worldwide renewal rates and new sign-ups also drove it. Free cash flow of $9.38B narrowly beat net income of $9,226 million in fiscal 2026 but not in 2025. Planned capex of about $7,500 million could narrow that. The margin and peer-growth claims were not judged. Cost ratios were stable, while comparable sales excluding gas and currency slowed to 7% from 8% amid intense competition. The hold case rests mainly on membership durability.
unknowns: Quarterly membership fee growth rates, which would show whether membership still outpaced total revenue (+11.1%) in the latest quarter
Membership fee growth excluding the September 2024 fee increase
Paid member counts and Executive membership penetration trends
Operating margin for the fiscal 2026 first quarter (ended around November 2025), the fourth quarter needed to verify the claim fully.
Quarterly segment-level operating margins, which could show whether any segment pressured the consolidated margin in an individual quarter.
Whether the quarterly operating margin figures are computed on total revenue or on net sales, since this affects comparability with the 3% threshold.
The exact free cash flow definition used by the backend figure (e.g., whether finance lease payments are deducted), which matters given the narrow margin.
Whether the working capital benefits (supplier payment terms, inventory turns) will persist.
The analyst's intended fiscal year, if not fiscal 2026.
Revenue and comparable sales growth rates of retail and warehouse-club peers for comparable periods
Whether Costco gained or lost market share
How peer growth compares after adjusting for gasoline prices and currency effects

Compare Costco's comparable sales growth excluding gas and currency against named retail peers over the same periods.
Track whether membership fee growth stays above sales growth as the fee-increase contribution fades.
Model free cash flow against net income under the planned fiscal 2027 capex of about $7,500 million.

analysis.corollary_rule: A corollary is an implication a model proposed and code computed. Each is read by the grammar and by the typed form the proposing model wrote: two readers, which is weaker than the two-of-three rule the thesis's own claims are read under. A corollary never moves a verdict; when most of a claim's computed corollaries come out against it, the claim is flagged.
analysis.audit_rule: A sentence is verified by code when every id it cites is in this run, at least one is evidence, and every number it writes is carried by that evidence: a verified finding's quotes and cited figures, an analytic's value, inputs and reading, a computed test's operands and result, a reported figure, an 8-K event's text. The claim's own words carry no number, and neither does the sentence a model wrote for a corollary: only what code computed for it does. A threshold is a third thing: when a number equals the threshold of a computed test or corollary the sentence cites, or a condition's own threshold, the sentence is not failed for it, and it is listed as a threshold restated, not checked as a fact. A bare year is carried by a cited item dated in that year. The audit does not decide whether a sentence follows from what it cites.
analysis.persistence_method: Resampling with replacement: 10,000 paths of 4 quarters, each step drawn from the measure's own last N quarterly changes (differences in points for a percent, growth rates for an amount), from the current value; the share of paths in which the test holds in every one of the 4 quarters. Seed 20261118. It assumes the past changes are exchangeable: it ignores trend, seasonality and anything not in the facts. It describes the history; it is not a forecast.

bottom_line.text: Three of the four claims are supported, yet none carries the decision to hold at this price: under the reverse DCF at the 2026-09-30 price, the enterprise value needs revenue to grow 17.3% a year for 10 years, against the +6.6% a year the company delivered over its last three fiscal years.

The growth claim the price most needs, outgrowing peers, is unjudged: the only peer evidence is a rank of 4 of 9 in 2025, and comparable sales excluding gasoline and currency slowed to 7% from 8%.
At 45.7x earnings and a 2.2% free cash flow yield, the supported cash claim adds little support for the price, because free cash flow cleared net income by only $156.0M.
The record cannot say how the $30 per share special dividend declared after the price date will be funded, or what it does to the balance sheet, because no filing after it is in the record.

A careful investor would next want to see two things: whether the quarterly operating margin moves past its 4.0% high toward the industry median of 5.0%, and whether operating cash flow absorbs the planned step-up of capital expenditure to about $7,500.
